text:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Customer AEGIS (dedicated pool eu-west-2) p99 latency breach. Current p99 = 3.8s (SLO 1.5s). Triggered at 2026-03-15T03:12Z. Incident ID: INC-20260315-0872. Paging oncall.

maria: I'm in. seeing sustained p99 spike, p95 also elevated. Traffic spike concentrated on tenant aegis-tenant-42 (VPC).

chen: acked. hopping on now. any recent deploys for dedicated runtime in eu-west-2?

maria: no infra deploys in last 60m. metrics: token-serving latency up, queue depth high on pool-gpu-eu2-01. KV cache hit rate dropped ~20%.

raj: tagging in for customer comms. @aegis_support are you seeing application-level retries or error rates from your side?

Aegis_support: We see elevated client-side timeouts around 03:08Z, retries increasing. No config changes on our end. Customer reports slow interactive UI for their internal reviews.

chen: ok. immediate mitigation plan: 1) isolate noisy tenant 2) scale dedicated pool temporarily 3) enable regional fallback to hosted model for non-sensitive routes 4) keep customer updated. Who can run tenant isolation?

maria: I can run the eviction + throttling command. Doing it in canary first.

maria: ```
# isolate tenant: mark tenant read-only + throttle
redwood tenant update --id aegis-tenant-42 --set throttle=20% --set mode=read_only --reason "p99 mitigation INC-20260315-0872"
# evict long-running sessions
redwood sessions evict --tenant aegis-tenant-42 --older-than 10m
```

maria: running now. will monitor.

oncall-bot: @chen, command accepted and started by maria at 03:18Z.

maria: eviction completed, throttle set. queue depth dropped ~30% within 90s. p99 down to 2.1s but still above SLO.

chen: good. proceeding to scale dedicated pool by adding 2 nodes to pool-gpu-eu2-01. scale command: ```
redwood pool scale --pool pool-gpu-eu2-01 --add-nodes 2 --type p4d
```

chen: queued, expected join time ~2m. also enabling prefix KV warm cache for common prompts for AEGIS.

raj: contacting Aegis primary: "we're applying temporary throttles and adding capacity. Can we route non-sensitive bulk/batch requests to Redwood-hosted fallback models to reduce load on your dedicated pool?"

Aegis_support: Ok to route non-PII endpoints. We'll confirm endpoints allowed. We'll also enable reduced concurrency on our client side. Thanks.

sophie: scale complete, nodes joined. p99 at 1.6s now. still watching p95 spikes, but overall latency trending down.

maria: leaving throttle in place for 10m stabilization window; preparing rollback steps. runbook note: if p99 < 1.5s for 10 consecutive minutes, remove throttle: ```
redwood tenant update --id aegis-tenant-42 --unset throttle --set mode=normal
```

chen: creating post-incident action items: - investigate root cause of cache hit rate drop - audit session hotspots for tenant - revisit autoscale thresholds for dedicated pools in eu-west-2 - consider tenant-slowdown circuit-breaker improvements

raj: I'll own customer follow-up summary + SLA impact calc. recording: incident start 03:12Z, isolation at 03:18Z, capacity add at 03:21Z, stable at 03:27Z.

maria: recording logs and traces to incident artifact INC-20260315-0872 on Confluence. adding perf samples.

incidents-bot: Incident INC-20260315-0872 updated: severity=sev2, status=mitigated, assignees=[maria, chen, raj].

Aegis_support: Thanks team, system performance restored for now. We'll keep monitoring and loop back in 1h for debrief.

maria: handing off to on-call followup shift. Chen, any other immediate actions?

chen: none immediate. I'll put watch for 45m then hand to daytime SREs. Marking thread with :white_check_mark:.

oncall-bot: Handoff recorded: next_oncall=day-sre@redwood at 04:12Z.

maria: closing war-room updates here. will file RCA draft after data collection. :memo:
